sections.h2: Does the City of Sarasota send its own tax bill?
sections.html:
No. A house inside city limits gets one bill from the county tax collector, and the city shows up on it as one of several taxing bodies. The county appraiser's value is the starting point for every line.

Expect city, county, school board and district charges to share the notice with non-ad valorem items for services like fire protection and trash. Start with the appraiser's property search to see your parcel, then open the collector's account page to see what has been billed. If you are selling, the county tax guide has the full calendar and our selling page for Sarasota covers offers and closing.

sections.h2: What does the City of Sarasota publish about Amendment 3?
sections.html:
Its property tax page reproduces the ballot summary. The text raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, then indexes it, and cuts the yearly cap on non-homestead assessment growth from 10 percent to 5 percent.

Newcomers are treated differently under the same text: anyone who is not a Florida resident on December 31, 2026 gets the current exemption first and the larger one from the fifth year. Local governments would also be limited to listed uses of property tax revenue, including public safety, schools, infrastructure and debt service. The summary gives January 1, 2027 as the effective date.

On the county side, the tax collector confirms that the 2026 notice is payable as issued and that the changes reach the 2027 bill. School taxes and non-ad valorem charges stay. Before pricing a house, ask the appraiser what the changes mean for your parcel.

sections.h2: What proof does a Sarasota homeowner need for homestead?
sections.html:
The appraiser asks for ownership evidence and residency evidence, plus information about any earlier home. You must be a Florida resident living in the house on January 1, and March 1 is the timely application date.

Ownership can be shown by a recorded deed, tax bill or TRIM notice. For residency, bring a Florida license or ID with the home address, and at least one of voter registration, vehicle registration or a recorded declaration of domicile. A second route uses two items from a different list: a W-2 or paystub, children's school registration, a federal tax return, or utility and bank records. If the old home is still yours, show that its exemption was cancelled; if you sold it, show the sale date.

  • Both spouses supply their details.
  • A Social Security number is required for each applicant under s. 196.011(1)(b).
  • A permanent resident who is not a citizen shows a green card.

sections.h2: What happens to the Save Our Homes cap when a Sarasota house sells?
sections.html:
It disappears for that owner. The cap limits yearly assessed growth to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and a sale lets the appraiser reset the parcel to just value the next January 1.

The state's cap chart, revised in January 2026, lists 3.0 percent for 2024, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. A family that has held a Sarasota home for decades can carry a large gap between assessed and market value, and the buyer starts without it.

Portability softens the blow for the seller. Set up a new Florida homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one, and file DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1. The statute text caps the transferred amount at the lesser of $500,000 or the old home's just-minus-assessed gap, and it notes 2026 amendments first apply to the 2027 roll.

sections.h2: Which Sarasota exemptions do not depend on living in the house?
sections.html:
Four $5,000 exemptions can be claimed on any one Florida property a permanent resident owns: widow or widower, total and permanent disability, blindness, and disabled veteran at 10 percent or higher.

Other benefits need homestead. Seniors of limited means may qualify for an added exemption, with income papers due June 1. A veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability may have homestead tax waived, and the benefit can pass to a surviving spouse.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Sarasota house that has back taxes?
sections.html:
Yes. The balance is cleared through closing, and the collector warns that tax left unpaid after April 1 turns delinquent and can cost the owner the property.

The buyer is accountable for the entire bill whenever the purchase happens. The seller's share rides on the settlement statement as a credit, rather than as a payment to the collector. A bill that reaches a former owner goes back to the new owner or to the collector. At the clerk's counter, the deed carries stamp tax of $0.70 per $100, rounded up, as the clerk's fee page prints. A long delinquency can lead to the process on our tax deed page.

sections.h2: What paperwork do Sarasota disability and widow exemptions need?
sections.html:
Each claim has its own proof, and the appraiser spells it out. Gather it before March 1 so a first-time filing is not delayed.

  • Widow or widower: an application, and possibly a copy of the death certificate. Remarriage ends the exemption.
  • Total and permanent disability: a Florida physician's certification on form DR-416, or a certificate from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
  • Blindness: a certificate from the state Division of Blind Services, the VA or the Social Security Administration, or a physician or optometrist form.
  • Disabled veteran: a letter, certificate or ID card from the government showing the rating.
  • Wheelchair or legally blind homestead exemption: two unrelated Florida physicians on DR-416, plus a Statement of Gross Income on DR-501A.

The income test for that last exemption counts VA benefits and Social Security, according to the appraiser's overview.

sections.h2: Where do Sarasota owners take a complaint about value or rates?
sections.html:
Value goes to the appraiser and then to the Value Adjustment Board, within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. In 2026 that mailing was August 17. Rates go to the budget hearings listed on the notice.

The board decides value, classification and exemption questions only. Florida's calendar puts tentative budget hearings in September and October and final hearings after that.

sections.h2: In what order should a Sarasota owner handle a tax problem?
sections.html:
Match each question to the office that owns it: value and exemptions to the appraiser, the bill to the collector, recorded paper to the clerk.

  • Open your parcel on the appraiser's search and view the 2026 TRIM through the button near the top of the record.
  • Check that exemptions survived any name or address change.
  • Look for a prior-year balance on the collector's account page.
  • Search the clerk's Official Records for liens.
  • Join the clerk's fraud alerts for the owner's name.

faqs.q: Does the City of Sarasota collect property tax itself?
faqs.a: No. The county tax collector bills for every taxing body inside the city, so you pay one notice.

faqs.q: What is the city millage rate for Sarasota?
faqs.a: The city sets its own rate, one line on your bill. Read your TRIM notice or ask the city or appraiser for the current figure.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead in Sarasota?
faqs.a: By March 1, having lived in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Late filings are still reviewed.

faqs.q: Does the Save Our Homes cap pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets assessed value to just value the next January 1, though portability may carry part of the benefit to your next Florida home.

faqs.q: Can I sell with unpaid taxes in Sarasota?
faqs.a: Yes, and the balance is normally settled from the proceeds at closing after the title agent confirms the amount.
